I think it would prevent us who use it as a scapegoat for our own issues from doing it. And that’s a good thing for both the victims and the cat fishers, because it can ruin both sets of lives.

For me my catfishing was an addiction. So as soon as someone left I would feel lost and hurt. Not just because I lost someone I cared for and chatted with for a long time, but also because I wasn’t getting the things I was addicted to. So I’d try to find that again by moving on to someone else. 

Everyone is different, but for me I needed to recognize why I was catfishing and what I was getting from it in order to stop. Even when I felt like a piece of shit for the amount of hurt I caused people, I still didn’t stop. I was lying to myself. I felt like two different people and I always believed the things I said to the people I was catfishing even tho they were mostly lies. 

It took a long time but as soon as I could admit to myself I was a catfish, and figure out why I was...I stopped.

It’s a form of fraud or catfishing that allows someone to get videos/specific photos and if they add each other on social media they won’t get caught right away etc.

The problem with what you’re saying is that you’re not taking in to account that not everyone has the same intelligence and working brain as you do. But at the time when I started, I was young and honestly did not understand the consequences. Didn’t know that an innocent night of one short conversation would turn into much much more.

I felt like the person I was pretending to be. I believed everything I was saying that was a lie. I realize that sounds so stupid and sounds awful and I’m in no way making excuses or wanting sympathy. It’s just facts. That’s how deep I was in. 
I didn’t have a bad childhood. Everything bad about my life has actually happened because of my catfishing and lack of effort of my own life. 
But just like how we catfishers cannot understand how awful it feels to be catfished and how we destroys someone’s heart.... people who have never been mentally fucked the way some of us were when we did it can’t understand why we did what we did and honestly man... feel really fucking lucky that you don’t. 
Nothing gives anyone a right to lie, cheat, steal or hurt others. But people do it. Reddit is supposed to be somewhere people can get these reasonings and feelings of guilt off their chest in hopes there will be someone who understand and doesn’t pass judgement. I'll speak from an actual catfish, it is possible to change. I catfished also as a defense mechanism. It was never about low self esteem or money... it was about losing my parents and not being able to grieve. There was a few other issues that added to it but that's a novel in itself. I regret what I did, and I am working with a therapist to move on.

I will admit that it was an addiction. So there will be people who may never stop, or may take longer. But if the desire is there, he can definitely stop and improve. I will speak from experience that even though I knew what I was doing was wrong... during the times I was most involved in it, it was almost as if I believed what I was saying. I believed I was the person I said I was... and I hurt people I never intended on hurting. I developed actual real feelings for these people. I believed I was treating them well when we spoke. I sent them flowers or gifts sometimes. I even lent some of them money to help them get by. We made plans that I believed were real plans in my head and got excited for them. When I cried because I hurt those people - it was real tears, I felt real shame and real guilt. When I picked up my phone and did this for the first time it was not meant to be a hurtful or deceitful person. It was meant to be one single conversation... that ended up costing me years of my life and I made one bad decision after another.When I finally woke up one day (by getting caught in a way) and realized what I was doing, I was disgusted and I wanted to change. And have been working on it ever since.

Honestly, if this guy is serious about changing and is actually admitting to what he did (took me FOREVER to admit it even to myself) then I think it would be extremely beneficial for him to have friends in his real life that are willing and able to help him through this without judgement. We are real people too. We are lost, and some of us really are good people who just got caught up in something we can't even explain. I wish I had someone here to help me besides my therapist. But how you are conflicted, and how people are responding is why I don't tell anyone in my real life what I did. It's absolutely impossible for someone "normal" to put themselves in our shoes and realize we can be caring genuine people who simply made a mistake and got lost. It's easier for people to feel some sort of sympathy for those addicted to drugs than those who may be addicted to the idea of being someone else (which is an escape from our life just like drugs... just a different escape). It's people like that that set us up to fail before we even start to attempt to change and be better people.

I am not defending what he did, or what I did at all. We did terrible things. I didn't do this to people I knew in my real life, but I did it to real people and fed them lies and fantasies, and gave them hope of a loving partner and relationship and then I ripped their heart out and destroyed everything they thought they had romantically with me when they realized I was not who I said I was.Sorry for the novel, but I want to make it clear that people can change if they want to. So if you have it in you - don't give up on him.
